question.worked_solution:
The integral is defined over a type II region.

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{\pi /4}}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{4}}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡{y}^{3}}{{y}^{2}}\,dx\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{\pi /4}}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡{y}^{3}}{{y}^{2}}[{\int }_{0}^{y}dx]dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{\pi /4}}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡{y}^{3}}{{y}^{2}}[x]_{0}^{{y}^{4}}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{\pi /4}}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡{y}^{3}}{{y}^{2}}({y}^{4}-0)\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{\pi /4}}{y}^{2}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡{y}^{3}\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{\pi /4}}{y}^{2}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡{y}^{3}\,dy & ={[\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{\pi /4}} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-0) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{6}\end{aligned}
$$
